result.topic_en: Euler fixes the integration constant Δ in Lagrange's integral of dx/√X ± dy/√Y = 0 by setting y = 0. He concludes that arcs of any curve given by Π:z can be added and compared like circular arcs, and begins treating the arc-doubling case y = x, where the formula becomes 0/0.

$\frac{2A+B(x+y)+2Cxy+Dxy(x+y)+2Exxyy\mp 2\sqrt{XY}}{(x-y)^2}=\Delta$.
Quare cum esse debeat $\Pi:x \pm \Pi:y = \Pi:k$, manifestum

vnde constans indefinita $\Delta$ eodem prorsus modo defini-

§. 66. Hinc si formulae $\Pi:z$ exprimat arcum cu-

items.english: It is clear that, setting y = 0, we must have Π:x = Π:k and hence x = k. From this the indefinite constant Δ is determined in exactly the same way as it was exhibited.

items.english: In this curve all arcs can be compared with one another in the same way as circular arcs are compared. Given two arcs Π:x and Π:y, a third arc Π:k can always be exhibited equal to either the sum or the difference of those arcs.
